title: Affine intersection acyclicity makes the module Cech beta augmentation a quasi-isomorphism
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $I$ be an index set, and let $U_i$ be a family of opens such that every intersection $U_{i_0} \cap \cdots \cap U_{i_n}$ is affine for $n\geq 0$. No covering condition is assumed. Let $F$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent], and let $F\to J^\bullet$ be any injective resolution [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Form the module-valued Cech complex and the double complex with resolution degree first as in [def-sc-module-cech-comparison]. Then the explicitly constructed augmentation $\beta:C^\bullet(U,F)\to\operatorname{Tot}(C^\bullet(U,J^\bullet))$ of that construction is a quasi-isomorphism: its homology map is an isomorphism in every nonnegative degree.

source.place: Affine vanishing input to Tag 01ET; beta of Tag 01EQ, proof, with first-quadrant column filtration as in Homology Lemma 12.25.4

proof.text: Apply affine open vanishing to F on each intersection (hU n y). This supplies precisely the Subsingleton hypotheses of [lem-sc-module-cech-resolution-columns].

Define a as the image of I.ι.f 0 under the Cech functor. Its composite with the resolution differential is zero by functoriality and the injective resolution augmentation equation. Apply [lem-sc-module-cech-resolution-columns] with that proof to get all column quasi-isomorphisms.

Apply [lem-sc-first-quadrant-column-augmentation] with K=moduleCechDouble U I, A=Cech(U,F), a, and b=moduleCechBeta U I. The component equality hb is reflexivity by the explicit beta definition. The theorem gives QuasiIso beta.

theorem moduleCechBeta_quasiIso_of_affine {X : Scheme.{u}} {ι : Type u}
    (U : ι → X.Opens)
    (hU : ∀ (n : ℕ) (y : Fin (n + 1) → ι), IsAffineOpen (⨅ l, U (y l)))
    (F : X.Modules) [SheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherent (R := X.ringCatSheaf) F]
    (I : InjectiveResolution F) : QuasiIso (moduleCechBeta U I)
